steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: A group of bandits who fled here... So Rhodes Island takes jobs like this too?

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Yep. Given our branch offices operate under all sorts of conditions all across the world, any weird and wild commission could come to our doors.

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: But it IS usually just responding to some Infected or Originium.

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: According to the info the office gave, the village militia'll help us with the operation. Says their chief's a pretty impressive one.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: We already spent a chunk of time just getting here. I hope nothing happened in the meanwhile...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: You're Rhodes Island, here to help us catch the bandits?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Yes, we are.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: You're the head of the village militia. Was Lanton the name?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: No, I'm his brother Landi. The thing with him, well...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Not long ago, while he was leading a team on patrol, they got attacked. The others were alright, but he went missing. We've searched for ages without turning up any trace of him, so now it's up to me to lead the militia until we get him back.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I'm sorry. If we'd only come a bit sooner...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: It's not your fault. It takes time for Messengers to pass the word on, after all.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I'm just hoping you can help out with catching those bandits. It'll take a weight off the village's shoulders.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Our intel says a group of bandits stole a merchant caravan's Originium weapons, and then fled this way.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: That tells us these bandits are no pushovers.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Right now, it's highly likely they're eyeing the village, so all of you stay here to protect against potential raids.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: But––

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: They're going, so it's up to us. No harm in that.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Gerain, those bandits are the reason my brother's missing now!

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: And? Lanton's the strongest in the village. If they can send him missing, what good'll we do if we go?

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: And what good'll you do, Landi?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I don't want an argument with you.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Only catching these bandits can bring peace to the village.

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: How? With your 'superior' command skills? No idea how we usually patrol, no idea how we even form our squads, is that all it takes?

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: Or your 'genius' leadership where you can't even remember all our names?

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: You can't seriously think you're Lanton, can you?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Come again?!

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: That's my point for today.

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: Do you think we see you as a decent stand-in for the captain? You're just a shame on Lanton, that's it.

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: You've never drilled with us, all you do is hunt in the mountains all day. The idea of protecting the village's never even occurred to you.

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: Lanton's gone, and you suddenly pipe up saying you'll be our militia chief in place of him? What good is you protecting the village going to do? What's going on in your head?

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: Look, you even made a point of carrying Lanton's sword. Who are you fooling?

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: Back me up here!

steps.name: Militiaman B
steps.text: He's right! I got fed up a long time ago.

steps.name: Militiaman C
steps.text: Damn straight. What gives you the right to boss us around, Landi?

steps.name: Militiaman B
steps.text: Alright, let's go, forget him!

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: There it is. Enough, Landi. Leave it to these outsiders.

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: They'll get a lot more done than you, that much's plain to see.

steps.name: Nightmare Knight
steps.text: Your dream is taken from another. Your conviction is borrowed.

steps.name: Nightmare Knight
steps.text: You use your young age as an excuse for your confusion... but what point is there?

steps.name: Nightmare Knight
steps.text: The world can laugh at the Radiant Knight's stubbornness, but no one may refute the strength in her actions.

steps.name: Nightmare Knight
steps.text: Yet you... you are not even a knight.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: No bearing on me if they don't go. I'll be following you.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: You'll need someone to show the way, right?

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Let him come with, Blemishine.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I haven't seen anyone fishy around this area, or any signs people stopped over.

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: Not bad, dude. Didn't think you could actually walk it on top of talking it.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: If you can't think about what to say, I suggest you keep your mouth shut.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: It's alright. Hunting really is the only thing I'm good for.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Let's go and check ahead.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Also... I'm sorry. For that whole scene you had to see.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: It's not that they're unwilling to help you, they're just not willing to help me.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Why are they so opposed to you?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Because... I guess because I've taken up my brother's post.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: My grandpa was the last militia chief. He trained Lanton and me when we were little.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: We're right on the border here. Bandits on the run, bounty hunters, you name it, they show up in droves. Once we were grown, Grandpa wanted us to protect the village from harm, together.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: But—I'm not even good at people like my brother is. I'm better off alone.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: It's like they said, I've never drilled with them. I just like hunting in the mountains on my own.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton understood how I felt, so he became militia leader.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: That was never a problem, up until he went missing.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: (Exhale)...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: The sword you're using now—that's your brother's?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: It's his saber. Apparently, it was found close to where he went missing.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I picked it up because I wanted to use it on those bandits who hurt him.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: This sword's too heavy for you. It's not a good fit for you at all.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: That's alright. I'll use it to make the bandits pay.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But––

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Watch out!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Hnph!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Who are you?!

steps.name: Bandit
steps.text: Dammit.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Hold it!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Wait, don't just run off!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Ugh, take them down first!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Stay where you are!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton, it's you, isn't it?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: ...Landi.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton, your clothes. The bandits who attacked us were wearing these.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: You've always been smart. You should be able to guess.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: This means you're working with those bandits...

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: I don't want to be trapped in a remote hellhole like that all my life, Landi.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: I don't want to spend my whole life bossing around some idiots forever.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: That's all there is to it.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton!

steps.name: Bandit
steps.text: Guh...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: That's a decent number of targets...

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Blemishine, leave this to us. You go find Landi.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: You probably have a bad feeling about this, just like I do.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Then go. Don't wait around to confirm that feeling.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Relax. We can handle this thing.

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: Sure can.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Got it!

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Landi, why are you holding my sword?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Didn't you always think my sword was too heavy? Always saying your dagger fit you better?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: You obviously know why.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: You weren't like this before.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Oh, I wasn't?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: This is how I should be, then.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: I always had to protect the village, to be a role model. I never truly let myself loose.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: I never experienced what it's like to mouth off at people.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: And now I know! It feels amazing!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Gngh...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I hear them talking. They're right in front...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Landi—

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: And you, Landi.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: You know, I've always wanted to be like you, no one's lives on my back, just me looking after myself, going into the mountains to hunt, day in, day out, right?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: And now, I know how you feel.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: It's great, absolutely great! No wonder you never got sick of it!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton, was it my fault you had to take up all that responsibility?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Maria, tell me the truth.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Did I rob you of your dreams?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Maybe.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: All I can tell you is I plan to experience a hell of a lot I never experienced before. Steal a thing or two, burn a building or three.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Maybe even... kill a couple people.
Lanton raises the knife in his hands, brandishing it at Landi without an ounce of hesitation.
As if it wasn't his younger brother before him, but a simple logjam blocking his way.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Stop!

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Hmph... your backup's here, huh.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: You'd kill your own brother?!

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Why not? I chose this path. He might be my brother, but right now he's in my way.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Landi, get up!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: You're supposed to protect the village!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I know this is partially my fault, that you turned into this. I'm so sorry.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: But if you're going to destroy the village over it... then I'll stop you.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I'm going to protect our village!

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Protect it?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: What are you talking about, Landi?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: When have you ever protected the village?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: What have you done for the village that gives you the right to talk yourself up like this?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Do Gerain and the rest put any faith in you? Do you know how to assign them? Do you know what a militiaman should do? You know jack squat.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: And even then, you've got the nerve to come up to me and say you're going to protect the village?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I'll learn how!

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: When? Now? Not going to happen, little brother.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Don't force your selfishness onto others!

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Stop her!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Ungh.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Landi, you ought to carry on with your little life.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: And after I destroy the village, you ought to run.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: You, standing here now, all righteous while you tell me things I used to say, pretending the dream I had is now yours...

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: You look absolutely ridiculous.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Why?! Am I wrong for wanting to protect the village?!

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: You're not wrong, you're just—

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: A little late to it.
With a 'clang,' the sword in Landi's hand breaks in two.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Guh... ahh...

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: No more dreaming, Landi.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Leave the village. Find somewhere new to live.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Landi...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Blemishine, am I really the one in the wrong?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Was it my fault for not sharing some of my brother's responsibility a bit sooner?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: For being so selfish, just looking after myself?
How should I answer him?
Should I tell him he's wrong? But is he really wrong?
Should I tell him he's right? But does he really believe it?

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: Blemishine! Are you guys alright?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: We're fine... what about over there?

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: I caught two suckers, and shook the position of the bandit stronghold from them. We can head there now to sweep them up, no problem.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: There are more of them than we estimated. With just the few of us, we probably have no way of clearing them out in one go.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: We need to head back and mobilize that village militia.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Alright. Let's go, then.
In a confined room, the sound of metal on metal rings with no respite.
With a serious look, Blemishine beats away at a metal chunk reddening, as if what she hammers into shape is her own will.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Margaret, what he asked his older brother, it's—surprising, actually, how similar it is to what you asked me.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: 'Did I rob you of your dreams?'

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But it's the other way round here, funnily enough.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Honestly, I feel like it's a mutual question.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I could say, in the past, it was me being obsessed with smithing that made you even more enthusiastic about the knight competitions.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: And when I say that, it's me blaming myself for losing you your right to choose.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I could also say it was your enthusiasm for knight competitions that led me to get so much more obsessed with smithing.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But when I say that, it seems like I'm blaming you for losing me my dreams.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: It's like it makes sense either way, and makes no sense either way.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I kind of understand now. People only put it in terms like these when they're trying to settle accounts.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: In times like these, everyone's just trying to push the guilt onto the other side. They don't actually consider things to be that way.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: In reality, how do you even say things like this straight?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: We grew up together, we impacted each other. That's how we came to understand each other.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Blemishine, are you forging a weapon?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: No, it's a sort of way to concentrate that I learned from a colleague named Vulcan.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: It's not to forge weapons, it's to purge my own distracting thoughts.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Do you want to try it too? It's really effective.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Ha ha, not this time.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I came to pass on word. Most of the militia are willing to join the bandit clear operation. The village is readying supplies and weapons right now.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: To be honest, you're a lot like me.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I have an older sister, myself.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: My sister's like your brother. She always shouldered a responsibility that, maybe, me and her should've taken on together.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: And I took her protection for granted, doing what I wanted to do.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: As a side note, what I like doing is smithing of all kinds, making all sorts of weapons and equipment. The armor I'm wearing now, I made myself.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: This hunk of metal's not bad. Let's go with it.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: It was all until one day, because of—certain reasons, my sister was forced to leave home, and go far, far away.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: It was only after that, I realized, how much she was shielding me.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I'm like you, too, trying to take on the responsibility she once took on for me.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Then... did you succeed?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I failed, eheh.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: When I tried to take that responsibility, I got so much criticism, but out of it all, I think what most cut to the core was—

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Someone said my dreams were borrowed.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I've never seen the sights my sister saw, and I've never walked the path she went.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: When things seemed like they were about to come crumbling down, it was only then I suddenly realized, oh—it seems like I should do something, and then I went to do it, and practically, I failed.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Hmm... this furnace is just too old! Once I'm done using it, I think I'll give it a revamp.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: My sister might say I did well, but I know in actuality, it was far from enough.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: The one way I'm luckier is... my sister came back in the end, and once again, she took up the responsibility she held before.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: And she does even more now, and even better.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: While my brother couldn't stand the burden, and chose to abandon his duty.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I already failed.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Why even tell me all this?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I've never regretted my obsession with smithing, and I don't feel my decision to pick up my sister's burden midway was wrong.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I'm hoping I can pass those ideas onto you.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I know I wasn't properly prepared, and I know I wasn't enough to walk the path she walked, in her shoes.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But even if I've experienced, and confirmed that for myself, I still feel proud of taking that step.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Maybe I couldn't get far down the way of the knight, but at least I know I didn't stray from my own beliefs.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: You're so strong.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Not at all. I'd crumple in training and beg Auntie Zofia to go easy on me, and I almost started crying when Margaret came back.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: And I had no time to work on my beloved smithing.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But—I don't consider blood ties, or family, or whatever other bonds like that to be an obstacle.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: So, when I've got no option except to take up the responsibility, I don't feel anything wrong with that.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: That's my answer.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I want to know yours.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I always enjoyed all that my brother gave me, took it for granted too.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: When I saw him like that, I felt guilty.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: But I'm part of this village, and I still want to protect it.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: It doesn't matter if I was called a slouch. It doesn't matter if I'm not trusted... I don't want these things to bring me regret.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: So... I guess what I mean is it's the least I can do to fight off my brother.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: But I don't know what to do...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Hand that broken sword over, here.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I'll forge you a weapon that fits you.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: That sword's too heavy for you. It'll make your center of gravity wildly unstable, and you won't have a good hold over the power.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: You can't deploy your full strength using a weapon that doesn't suit you.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: If my sister was here, she'd head the charge on their camp. She'd topple every last one of them.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But I'm a craftsman, and the way craftsmen help others, is by putting the best tools in their hands, making them stronger still.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Margaret, in some sense, aren't these brothers just us from another timeline?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: One where you renounced the path of knighthood, wandered the four corners of the land.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: And I took on your ideals for real, and I became a true knight.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Wow, just what kind of world would that've been? I can't imagine you having fallen at all, and I can't picture me becoming a real knight either.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But the knight novels have those sorts of knights too, who've fallen from grace while still holding fast to their creeds. That also seems really cool, in a way.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Ugh. Purge my thoughts, purge my thoughts.

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: I heard the story. Lanton's...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Gerain, I'm sorry...

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: What are you sorry for? He betrayed us, so now, he's the enemy. Simple as that.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Gerain, from today, I'll be joining you for training.

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: What's this? You can't still be treating yourself like Lanton now?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I'm not treating myself like him. I'm just treating myself as this village's militia chief.

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: Whatever.
Several days later...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Hah!

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: Whew, that's some tricksy blade.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Can you block him?

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: Sure. But those last few moves just now, at the very least they're closing on an investigative operator's standard.

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: Blooming like this in just a few short days, we could refer him to join us if we get the chance.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Ohh, I'm having a little flashback to the time Auntie Zofia was training me...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: How did she throw moves at me, again... ah, right, like this, probably!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Take this!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Ngh...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Plus my own follow-up!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Blemishine, to be honest, I'm already more or less used to the effects of your Arts.

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: Look at him, he puts on a pretty good show when he fights serious.

steps.name: Militiaman B
steps.text: Seriously, what's Landi been doing coming to train with us the last few days?

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: Hmph. It's what he should've been doing all along.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Right here!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Shame I already figured you'd gotten used to it. That's why I readied my posture way in advance!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But you've shaped up massively, haven't you!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Let's go again!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Hold on, come with me.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Here. It's the longsword I forged for you.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: It's just like Lanton's...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Yep, I made it according to that form~ Try wielding it a little.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: So light...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: How is it? Feels a lot easier to use, right?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I really don't know how I should thank you...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: It's alright, don't worry! I'm just glad seeing you cheer up!

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Now then, let's set out, and get all those bandits dealt with!

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Hmph, you came after all.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: You don't seem surprised.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: We need time to prep resources to attack the village, you need time to prep resources to wipe us out. It's a game of speed.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: You've won, that's all. Nothing to be surprised at there.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Leave the others to us. He's yours, Landi.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Looks like you chose to take on my burden... Here I thought, after breaking that sword, you could find some freedom too.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I won't judge you, Lanton. But—I don't think you can truly gain freedom by running away from your responsibilities.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: That's just because you haven't fled far enough. Haven't gone all the way.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Hm? Your weapon...

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: A noble tailored it for me after reforging your sword. From here on, I'll use it to protect our village.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Oh... good swordsmanship. You've improved some.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Do you know what it means to take on those responsibilities?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: You'll become a symbol to all the people, a mouthpiece of so-called protection, a personification of justice, so on. The one thing not included is you yourself.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Your life'll be a hundred times more painful than it used to be.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: And none of this was yours. And it shouldn't be yours either.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Since I was young, I've been determined to become that. And I chose to give up in the end, while you just lifted the ideal from my hands midway. How long can you bear it?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I regret it a lot, Lanton. I should've talked with you sooner, shared in your feelings. And maybe, after we understood each other better, none of this would've turned out the way it has.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: You ask me how long I can bear it. I'm going to try my hardest to avoid using the word 'bear.'

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I'll strive to work hard with the others, and turn endurance into fondness, into enjoyment.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I don't know if I can do it, but I want to try.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: You want to say you'll do better than me.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: There's no reason to compare the two of us.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: Drop dead.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: Got them all tied up. That ought to put a bow on things.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: So? What do you plan to do with me?

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton, are you really not going to change your mind?

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: The moment I decided to do this, I became a different person.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: You can treat me like a stranger and off me. I love you, Landi, and that's the last thing I can do for you as your older brother.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: This whole month, I've done a lot of things I never did before. I've drawn a joy from it I never knew in the past twenty-something years.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: I may not be satisfied, but it's enough.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: ... (Unties)

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Go, Lanton.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: The farther, the better.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Don't look back, don't come back, don't regret it.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Or else, I'll kill you.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I'm sorry, Lanton.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: If you looked back, I wouldn't have killed you.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: But if I really did just let you go like this, so many more people would've died.

steps.name: Elder Hunter
steps.text: It's how... it should be...

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: He was in the right, Blemishine.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I know...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I just never imagined, things could—reach this point, between family.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I'm sorry, Rhodes Islanders. I had to do this.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: We understand.

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: Give him a proper burial.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: ...I'll help you.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Lanton, this was the place you loved to train with your sword. I'll bury you here.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I don't know if I can become a militia chief as mighty as you were.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: But I'll try my hardest.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I'm very thankful to all of you Rhodes Islanders. Without you, I really have no idea how things would've turned out.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: The militia are all waiting for you. You've truly become their new leader. Go say a few words to them.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: Listen up, everyone.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: What my brother's done, I won't try to argue for him.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: The man I was is a far cry from him, you could see that, and I know that much. I was lazy, idle, and didn't do what I should've.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: But—I'm part of the village too.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: It's my wish to see the village improve, to protect it.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: From here on, in place of my brother, I'll take up the responsibility of protecting the village.

steps.name: Young Hunter
steps.text: I hope you will all support me!

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: ... (Clapping)

steps.name: Militiaman B
steps.text: I wasn't convinced before, Landi, but I think I've come over today!

steps.name: Militiaman A
steps.text: Landi, give it what you've got! I'll watch your back!

steps.name: Guard Operator
steps.text: Blemishine, what's up? Relief all over your face.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I always had some lingering fears.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I always thought me and my sister getting along was as natural as anything, and it would carry on just like that.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But now I know. I've just been lucky enough...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: If at the time, I actually did fluke my way into winning the whole thing, and when Margaret came back, I'd turned into an outstanding competition knight—

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Would I have become her enemy, maybe?

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I have no idea.

steps.name: Caster Operator
steps.text: Don't go thinking about it.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I know, I know.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Standing where I am, I've already realized, what I was thinking would probably never happen...

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: Because I'd never, ever end up in that position.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: The old me would say it's because she suits it better than I do.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: But now, I'd like to say it's because—I know that being where I am suits me better.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: I don't need the spotlight shone on me. If she can carry the equipment I've cast for her to stand in that light, that's enough for me.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: If she wants a sword, then I'll forge her the sharpest sword. If she wants a shield, I'll forge her the sturdiest shield.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: If she wants a way, then, well, I'll forge her the best tools to open it.

steps.name: Blemishine
steps.text: That's all there is to it.
